title: Improve tensor-parallel collectives and NCCL tuning to overlap comm/compute for multi-GPU serving
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: Reduce end-to-end latency and tail latency for multi-GPU tensor-parallel model serving by improving collective ops scheduling and tuning NCCL parameters so we can better overlap communication with local GPU compute. This addresses repeated customer reports of increased 95/99p latency for long-context workloads when using TP=2/4 and when autoscaling triggers device rebalancing. Changes: 1) Introduce a new schedule layer in the runtime that issues nonblocking NCCL collectives earlier and defers local compute until communication tokens are in flight; 2) Expose NCCL tuning knobs via runtime config (NCCL_ASYNC_PROGRESS, NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME, NCCL_IB_HCA) with sane defaults for our infra; 3) Add a lightweight rendezvous/ordering barrier to ensure tensor sharding reduces memory copies and enables CUDA streams to overlap comm/compute; 4) Optimize all-gather/all-reduce kernel launch parameters and add a micro-batching path that fuses short sequences to improve bandwidth utilization; 5) Add unit and integration tests, and a new perf canary that exercises TP=4 with long context (8k tokens) and burst QPS. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed in ENG-1623 - [x] Unit tests for schedule and NCCL wrapper - [x] Integration test (multi-GPU on canary infra) - [x] Perf benchmarks and regression checks - [x] CI green on main matrices - [x] Backwards-compatible config defaults Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged unless admin flips runtime.nccL.tuning.enabled or increases tp_comm_overlap flag. Risks and mitigations: enabling async NCCL progress on some kernels caused hangs in older drivers; we gate by driver and CUDA version checks and fall back to synchronous path when unsafe. Benchmarks: microbench (tp=4, batch=8): 95p latency reduced 28% (from 210ms to 152ms) and throughput increased 18% on our n1-standard-gpu nodes. End-to-end serving (8k context, burst QPS): p99 reduced 32% and cost-per-token reduced ~12% due to improved utilization. Testing: ran the canary perf-lab across 3 regions and validated KV cache correctness and token-level consistency with golden outputs. Rollout plan: staged rollout to dedicated clusters first, then hosted with canary routing for 5% traffic, monitor traces/alerts during 48h. Related: fixes a regression found in ENG-1704 where all-gather was serialized causing extra memcpy. Notes: some drivers require kernel parameter adjustments; ops team will schedule rolling driver updates.
